comments.content:
I see that's interesting. It's hard to say what's the right answer but I think we should not support sybils. To use the system you should only be using one GitHub account. There will be an incentive to use a single account when we have XP one day. 
You can make the error message clear, saying that the wallet is already registered. I suppose we can also make a note that they can unset their wallet address on the old account before setting on their new account in case they want to change the account that they use?

It's useful for us to know who is a sybil. Maybe unsetting can be like
/wallet null

They have had problems registering their wallet in the past so that may also be related. 
Lastly we still need to adjust the algorithm to not take a baseline from the formatting score. If relevance is 0 then the final score should be 0

We have come a long way in a few months.  
There were a lot of problems when that was posted and I suppose I figured that would have been the quickest solution to slightly more accurate scoring. These days I think the scoring is much more accurate. 
Semi related to that but relevance currently doesn't understand image contents. Check this spec, specifically for vector embeddings but maybe we should write in the HTML comments the descriptions of the images? 
- https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-vector-embeddings/issues/58
It could also be really interesting to pull the text contents from links to also score their relevance.
This should be discussed in the [dedicated task](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/issues/215)

Registration failures makes the system unusable. 
# Unnecessary Error
The previous error above it is sufficient this one should not display to the user. 
```diff
! Error: Error: No wallet address found
```
_Originally posted by @ubiquity-os[bot] in https://github.com/ubiquity/business-development/issues/85#issuecomment-2516869446_
# Registration Failure
```diff
! Error: [object Object]
```
_Originally posted by @ubiquity-os[bot] in https://github.com/ubiquity/business-development/issues/85#issuecomment-2516896879_
Code looks fine just need to include my QA comment adjustments. Basically adjust the posted comments.
You can probably set it to null.
I realized that this double hyphen is really only geared towards programmers. We should support only /wallet unset syntax for everybody

comments.content: Yes locations metadata caused things to be unnecessarily complicated. It is also even more obsolete now that we use GraphQL (it does not require that we pass in the org/repo name to fetch from issues/pulls)

Did you test that this works? My original belief was that we would clobber their existing wallet but this approach seems more correct especially for audits- being able to save every wallet. But as an extension of that logic it might make sense to have a record of all the IDs historically for any user too? 
One other edge case problem to consider but when I demo this capability I set mine to ubq.eth then back to mine. If I do this, then I'll have a lot of redundant entries.
I left some feedback there https://github.com/Meniole/command-wallet/issues/8#issuecomment-2535611748

comments.content: isn't this already handled by the SDK?
isn't `PATCH` method used by Supabase for updating a record? (below is a patch handler for wallets that updates it)
I think you could throw the logger error and SDK would post it as a comment
didn't we stop using location metadata? @0x4007

Not sure if this was intended but this change means that 2 Github accounts will able to use a same address because you search if wallet exists and update user's wallet id to that id. 
Before it checked if user's wallet id exists and tried to create a wallet entry if it didn't which failed on unique constraint, but now it checks for all wallet entries so if one exists it will just update the id.

It would be nice to also include this option in parameters somehow so the LLM can trigger this.
Maybe a boolean `unsetWallet`?
This function doesn't update anything though?

Yeah currently it's not auto-generated, we can add that later.
Hopefully LLM can use the function correctly, it might be confusing to the LLM because when you use `unsetWallet` it doesn't know whether to fill `walletAddress` with anything or not.

All wallets get saved but once the user changes it or unsets it, we lose the connection between wallet and user so we could add a userId to the wallet along with start and end date so we can have a history of all wallets and when they were used
There won't be redundant entries because it searches for existing wallet and just updates `wallet_id` on the user with existing wallet `id`. However if we implement it like I said above that would cause many entries if you're testing
